Assuming the two pendulums follow the following functions of their displacement :

θ1 = θ0 sin (ωt + ϕ1) ..(i)

and θ2 = θ0 sin (ωt + ϕ2) ..(ii)

As it is given that amplitude and time period being equal but phases being different.

Now, for first pendulum at any time t

θ1 = θ0 (Right extreme)

From Eq. (i), we get

⇒ θ0 = θ0 sin (ωt + ϕ1)

or 1 = sin (ωt + ϕ1)

or ω t + ϕ 1 = π 2 … iii

Similarly, at the same instant t for pendulum second, we have

θ 2 = - θ 0 2

Note θ0 = 2o is the angular amplitude for the second pendulum the angular displacement is one degree therefore, θ 2 = θ 0 2  and negative sign is taken to show for being left to mean position

From Eq. (ii), then

- θ 0 2 = θ 0 sin ω t + ϕ 2

⇒ sin ω t + ϕ 2 = - 1 2

⇒ ω t + ϕ 2 = - π 6 or 7 π 6

or ω t + ϕ 2 = - π 6 or 7 π 6 … iv

From Eqs. (iv) and (iii), the difference in phases

ω t + ϕ 2 - ω t + ϕ 1 = - 7 π 6 or π 2 = 7 π - 3 π 6 = 4 π 6

or ϕ 2 - ϕ 1 = 4 π 6 = 2 π 3 = 1 2 0 ο
